content: 1. The drug tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) reduces the levels or effects of letermovir by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration of letermovir with P-glycoprotein inducers is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be considered. 2. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, the daily dose of levomilnacipran should not exceed 80 mg. Otherwise, alternative drugs should be considered. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor, increase lorlatinib to the previous dose after three plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 7. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 8. Elvitegravir and lovotibeglogene autotemcel interactions require discontinuation of antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous lurbinectedin dose. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid co-administration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine due to potential increased toxicity. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with intranasal midazolam can cause higher systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, monitor midostaurin for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 13. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 14. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 15. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 17. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 18. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 21. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 23. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If no alternative treatment exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 32. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. 33. Cobicistat increases the toxicity of ozanimod by increasing the exposure of its active metabolites through BCRP inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 36. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 38. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of perampanel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pexidartinib dose. 41. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 42. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. 43. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 44. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If necessary, monitor for lack or loss of virologic response. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the pimavanserin dose to 17 mg/day. 46. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. CYP3A inducers may reduce elvitegravir plasma concentrations, leading to loss of therapeutic effect and potential resistance. 47. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. 48. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 49. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 50. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 51. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 52. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 53. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 54. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 55. Cobicistat increases the levels of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with atazanavir and cobicistat in patients taking quetiapine should be avoided. If necessary, reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth of the current dose and monitor for quetiapine-associated adverse reactions. Refer to quetiapine prescribing information for initial dosing and titration. 56. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 57. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Co-administration with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors should be avoided. 58. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. 59. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used.
